muffen.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German muffen (“to have a moldy smell”), of uncertain ultimate origin, but possibly related to modder (“mud”), from Proto-Germanic *muþraz (“sediment”). However, compare Old High German *muff (“mold”).

s: to apply sleeves to or in sleeve technique
smelly, stinking, particularly: having a moldy smell
uninviting, fusty, in need of renovation
muffig.et: The senses "smelly" and "grumpy" go back to different origins. The former pertains to Muff (“bad smell”) from Middle Low German muffen; the latter to Muffel (“grumpy person”), which is an Upper German dialect word of unknown origin. In contemporary German both…

s: a Muslim, particularly one wearing religious attire
Mufti.et: Borrowed from Arabic مُفْتٍ (muftin), definite اَلْمُفْتِي (al-muftī), the active participle of أَفْتَى (ʔaftā, “to deliver a formal opinion”).

s: muff (piece of fur or cloth, usually with open ends, used for keeping the hands warm)
Muff.et: From older Muffel, from Dutch muffel, from Old French moufle, Medieval Latin muffula.

s: Unter den Talaren – Muff von 1000 Jahren
Under the academic dresses – mouldy smell of 1000 years

Muffe.et: A Low German variant of Muff.
